messages:
lina: quick RFC follow-up — thinking about a tenant opt-in path for compatibility shims instead of a global flag. want a short sync.

sam: +1, curious about runtime cost. are we talking header toggle or tenant metadata?

lina: leaning tenant metadata (stored in control plane) + a header emitted by gateways. avoids clients having to opt-in explicitly during rollout.

ben: how does that work with cached prefixes / kv cache? different behavior per tenant could fragment caches.

maria: big concern — if the shim changes tokenization/embeddings shape, cache hit rate drops. need to measure hit degradation, not just CPU cost.

sam: can we make shim deterministic and cache-aware? e.g., include opt-in hash in cache key so isolation is explicit.

lina: yes, plan A: include compat_version tag in cache key. downside: doubles KV entries for active tenants during transition.

ben: Ops-wise doubling cache entries is painful on prod GPUs. might prefer translation at the edge (gateway sidecar) so model-serving sees normalized payloads and cache unaffected.

maria: edge translation buys us cheaper scaling but raises latency at the gateway and complicates rollout ordering (edge -> runtime).

sam: tradeoff summary: control-plane toggle + in-runtime shim = simpler ordering, higher backend cost. edge-sidecar translation = lower backend cost, more complex routing and latency.

arch-bot: suggestion: add a telemetry tag "compat.opt_in" and a metric for cache_hit_rate_by_compat to quantify impact during canary.

lina: good call. we should also track token-per-request delta and tail-latency p95 for opt-in tenants.

ben: timeline proposal: implement control-plane opt-in + compat_version cache-key for short-term. run 2-week canary on 5 tenants. if cache hit drops > 20% then switch to edge translation for those tenants.

maria: +1 to canary. also recommend audit logs when the control plane toggles a tenant — compliance needs that for enterprise customers.

sam: small implementation note: control-plane schema change: add tenant.compat_opt_in: {version: string, expires_at: iso}. gateway will read that and append header "X-RW-Compat: v2.1".

lina: sample control-plane patch snippet: ```json
{"tenant_id":"t-123","compat_opt_in":{"version":"v2.1","expires_at":"2026-06-01T00:00:00Z"}}
```

lina: sample gateway passthrough: ```bash
curl -H "X-RW-Compat: v2.1" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
```

arch-bot: add automated prune job suggestion: remove compat entries after expires_at + 30d and emit deprecation_notice metric.

ben: ops ask: estimate cost impact of doubling cache keys for 5 tenants during canary. i can do ballpark if you give QPS.

lina: assigning action items: ben -> cost estimate + backend impact; sam -> control-plane schema + auth checks; maria -> telemetry dashboard (cache_hit_rate_by_compat, p95_lat, tpr_delta); me -> implement gateway header read + propagate. aim to start canary next Monday.

sam: noted. i'll PR the schema change today.

maria: I'll stub dashboards and add alert if cache hit delta > 15% or p95 increases > 50ms.

ben: will post numbers by EOD tomorrow.

lina: thanks — keeping this lightweight so we can iterate. we should capture long-term plan in RFC: edge translation option + deprecation prune policy. I'll draft and tag folks. :thumbsup:

arch-bot: reminder: add opt-in audit events to retention policy matrix.
